hook.text: Airbnb let hosts cross-post their listings to Craigslist automatically. Craigslist had the traffic.

buildup.text: Piggybacking means building on top of an existing platform's user base instead of starting from zero.

discovery.text: Zynga grew FarmVille through Facebook's social graph. Facebook's users became Zynga's users overnight.

twist.text: The host platform eventually fights back. Facebook cut Zynga off; Craigslist blocked Airbnb's API.

climax.text: Piggybacking gives explosive early growth but creates dependency. You must migrate users to your own.

punchline.text: Borrow someone else's audience. Just don't depend on it forever.

quiz.question: Why is piggybacking risky as a long-term strategy?
options: The host platform can cut off access

details.summary: Piggybacking is a growth strategy where a new platform leverages the existing user base of an established platform to acquire users rapidly. PayPal grew by embedding itself in eBay listings. Zynga piggybacked on Facebook's social graph. Airbnb listed properties on Craigslist.
details.whyItMatters: Piggybacking is one of the fastest paths to critical mass for new platforms. By tapping into a larger platform's distribution, startups can acquire millions of users before the host platform recognizes the threat and closes the door.
takeaways: New platforms grow by leveraging established platforms' user bases
Tactics include API integration, cross-posting, and embedded experiences
Host platforms often close piggybacking channels once they recognize the threat

faq.question: How did Airbnb use piggybacking to grow its supply?
faq.answer: Airbnb built tools that automatically cross-posted listings to Craigslist, where millions of users already searched for short-term rentals. This channeled Craigslist's massive audience to Airbnb listings. Craigslist eventually blocked the integration.

faq.question: What are the risks of a piggybacking growth strategy?
faq.answer: The host platform can shut off access at any time by changing APIs or terms. Over-dependence on a single distribution channel is fragile. The relationship is inherently adversarial once the host recognizes threat. Companies must transition to organic growth quickly.
